newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed, PGMs up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed, PGMs up.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were expected to open mixed Monday, with gold and silver seen slightly lower but platinum-group metals seen climbing further in line with another sharp jump in Japan overnight.
COMEX December gold was called unchanged to down $0.20 from Friday's close of $328.90 an ounce after trading from $329.50 to $328.00 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $323.80/30 early compared to the London morning fix of $324.05 and the New York close Friday of $324.40/90.

But gold and silver are still seen capped by a further rise in the dollar overnight to a new seven-year high against the mark, a fresh four-year high against the Swiss franc and a new seven-year high in its trade-weighted index.

COMEX warehouse gold stocks were unchanged at 914,011 ounces Friday, while COMEX silver stocks fell a further 530,732 ounces to 169,078,681 ounces, the lowest level since the addition of the Wilmington Trust stocks in January.
COMEX September silver was called unchanged to down 0.5 cent from Friday's close of $4.470.
But NYMEX October platinum was called up $1.00 to $2.00 from the previous close of $438.50, with NYMEX September palladium expected up $3.00 to $5.00 from Friday's finish of $206.60.
PGM futures surged even higher on TOCOM overnight for the fourth day in a row, as shortcovering continued, with spot market sales of PGMs by Russia not meeting pent-up demand, traders said.
